title: God is DEAD and so are you: Mankind's Fall from Grace into a Faithle
summary: An Educated Barbarian episode on Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil covering how God died: the slave revolt against the pain of faith, the spirit of the race, the shift from gratitude to fear, and atheism as Christianity's natural continuation. He argues modern people kept religion's subjection and morality while losing faith, and now worship money, celebrities or nothing.
claims: Faith is the frustration of basic instincts; suffering is bearable when you understand its purpose, and the weak revolted because they could not
Modern secular morality is religion stripped of spirituality, kept by governments and societies as a tool to organize and restrain people
The Church's historic role was to tame and domesticate European barbarians

Following Nietzsche's 'spirit of the race', he argues Latin peoples are predisposed to fervent Catholicism and northerners to unbelief, citing Latin American worship, Scandinavian atheism and Protestantism's German birth
Ancient Greek and early Christian religion centered on gratitude; it was replaced by fear when plebeian tastes overtook the aristocracy's
Most Christians he meets in his Christian country follow out of family and social pressure rather than choice, making their faith shallow
Be a god-fearing man, whose faith rests on gratitude, not a man-fearing god who worships only because he has no choice
He personally follows the New Testament and cannot relate to the Old, whereas Nietzsche saw binding the two together as a sin against the spirit
By eradicating paganism and disenchanting the world, Christianity created fact-only humans who could no longer accept its own miracles
Atheism is the natural continuation of Christianity: each unanswerable question takes the believer one step down the staircase toward unbelief
Humans only follow superiors; depicting God in human form and making him approachable devalues him, which is why some religions forbid representation
Modern religion kept the subjection and fear but lost faith's satisfaction, which is slave morality; strong men abandon it once given power
Trying to prove religion scientifically opens the door to endless questioning and creates atheists
Refusing the absurd kills faith; Nietzsche's 'God is dead' was regretful, not gloating

Nietzsche's three stages of religious cruelty: human sacrifice, the moral epoch of sacrificing one's instincts, then sacrificing God himself; religions that keep sacrifice and difficulty remain intact
Stoicism amounts to shaming instincts and is hypocritical, since nature is not calm or non-violent
Humans always worship something; today the biggest religion is money, and atheism, as belief in nothing, is nihilism, which is worse than believing in something wrong
